question: A cooperative society increases the annual rate of simple interest from 10% to 16frac1{2} %, then the yearly income of a person increases by ₹1,077.70. The simple interest (in₹) on the sum at 10% for four years will be:
solution:
**Given:**

Initial rate of simple interest = 10%

New rate of simple interest = 16¹/₂% = 16.5%

Increase in yearly income = ₹1,077.70

Time = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (S.I) = Principal × Rate × Time / 100

**Calculation:**

Let the Principal amount be P.

Increase in yearly income is due to the increase in rate:

Yearly income at 16.5% - Yearly income at 10% = ₹1,077.70

⇒ (P × 16.5 / 100) - (P × 10 / 100) = ₹1,077.70

⇒ P × (16.5 - 10) / 100 = ₹1,077.70

⇒ P × 6.5 / 100 = ₹1,077.70

⇒ P = ₹1,077.70 × 100 / 6.5

⇒ P = ₹16,580

Now, calculate Simple Interest at 10% for 4 years:

S.I = P × Rate × Time / 100

⇒ S.I = ₹16,580 × 10 × 4 / 100

⇒ S.I = ₹6632

**Simple Interest on the sum at 10% for 4 years is ₹6,632.**
